title: Q1 Roadmap Launch Readiness + Incident Review
summary: Internal postmortem on the recent latency regression observed during the canary rollout of v1.8 autoscaling. Decided on immediate short-term mitigations, ownership for bisecting the regression, and a tightened pre-rollout checklist. Aligned on next steps for Q1 launch readiness and documentation required for the security audit.

Nate to prepare canary rollback runbook and emergency scripts - due 2026-12-28

Samir to update Q1 roadmap gantt with new dependency windows - due 2026-12-29
Miles to run extended QA load tests on canary config and share logs - due 2027-01-06
action_items: Laura Gomez - perf bisect (look at kernel selection + batching) (due 2027-01-05)
Nate Brooks - canary rollback + emergency ops checklist (due 2026-12-28)
Miles Johnson - extended QA load + regressions matrix (due 2027-01-06)

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~77 minutes
Attendees: Samir, Laura, Nate, Priya, Miles, Zoe
---
[00:00] Samir: alright folks, uh thanks for joining  this is the Q1 roadmap launch readiness and postmortem for the latency regression we saw on the v1.8 canary. I'll kick off with quick context, then Laura will go into infra findings, Nate will cover the incident response, Miles will go over QA results, and we'll close with action items.
[00:18] Laura: cool, quick note, transcription may be off on some infra terms, you might see k V cache as K V cash or similar, so just flagging that now.
[00:28] Samir: yeah thanks. quick context  last wednesday we pushed v1.8 to the canary pool for dedicated autoscaling improvements. The canary target was about 5% of traffic, we saw a 12 to 18% token latency bump on P50 for request types with long context, and a handful of customer-facing errors when the KV cache warmed. That pushed us to roll back the canary mid-run.
[00:52] Laura: to add, initial traces show an unexpected kernel selection path on one node type, looks like a codepath that triggers suboptimal matmul kernels when sequence lengths vary widely. Could be due to the new compilation heuristic we landed.
[01:12] Nate: yeah during the canary we also observed higher GC in the runtime, or what looked like GC spikes  or actually mempressure-triggered housekeeping, so there's a mem/cpu interplay that amplified p99s.
[01:30] Miles: QA observed flaky chat sessions  about 3% partial outputs where stream closed early. Logs reference checkpoint write timeouts during heavy prefix cache churn. we have raw logs in the shared drive. link: shortlink/SCR-logs (note: placeholder)
[01:50] Priya: from a comms POV, we need to be careful, we already scheduled prerelease notes  pausing that until we have a concrete remediation or rollback rationale.
[02:05] Zoe: ops note  our canary routing had fallback to a different region which made debugging harder since we saw mixed hardware in traces. recommend pinning canaries to a single zone next time.
[02:20] Samir: okay, main questions for the group: is this regression 1) code-level (compiler/kernel) 2) config-level (batching, KV cache params) or 3) infra-level (node types/region mix)? Laura?
[02:34] Laura: initial bisect points to compiler heuristic change in the optimizer flag we toggled. but we can't rule out the batching change, because we also changed continuous batching thresholds. likely a combination.
[02:48] Nate: plus the mempressure interplay  some node types with lower GPU memory and different kernel fallback logic exposed this. so yeah multi-factor.
[03:05] Samir: ok let's walk timeline: who triggered rollback and why  Nate?
[03:12] Nate: Ops initiated a manual rollback after seeing degradation exceed SLOs for 10m and partial stream errors increased. Manual because automatic fallback wasn't configured for that metric.
[03:25] Samir: okay  missed opportunity there. automation should've handled it. add to action items.
[03:32] Miles: quick note on QA tests  our load profile didn't hit the exact seq-len distribution customers use; test harness needs to include wider seq-length tails. I put a draft test matrix in the drive.
[03:46] Priya: on security and compliance  the security audit people asked for the rollout checklist and change control docs for SOC2 evidence. we should ensure those get attached to the release. are we aligned on what's missing?
[04:00] Zoe: Audit wants a pre-rollout runbook + signoff chain. we had a signoff but it lacked perf smoke results for this config.
[04:14] Samir: OK immediate mitigations discussed: 1) pin canary to single zone to avoid mixed-node hardware 2) revert the compiler heuristic flag in the staging branch 3) tighten canary monitoring and add automated rollback on token-latency SLOs 4) update QA harness to include heavy seq-length tails. who's on each?
[04:35] Laura: I'll take compiler flag revert and run a controlled compile matrix.
[04:39] Nate: I'll own the rollback automation and runbook plus ops scripts.
[04:43] Miles: QA harness and extended load tests, I'll own.
[04:46] Priya: comms + stakeholder timeline.
[04:50] Samir: great. next, deeper discussion on root cause details  Laura, can you summarize the kernel selection evidence?
[05:00] Laura: so we saw that for certain seq-len distributions, the new heuristic chooses a smaller tile size which interacts poorly with the quantized path; kernel fallback then runs slower matmul kernels. the traces show extra copy ops and mem thrash. transcription may have mis-typed some op names like fma vs vma.
[05:28] Nate: and those slower kernels increase GPU occupancy, which delays KV cache maintenance and causes prefix cache churn to block stream flushing.
[05:40] Miles: result is partial outputs seen by customers when stream flush times out. we captured p50/p95 increases, artifacts attached.
[05:55] Samir: Are any customer-facing configs we rolled out contributing? e.g., batching changes?
[06:02] Laura: we did reduce batching latency threshold to favor lower tail latency, but in edge cases that made micro-batches with variable seq-length which, combined with the heuristic, triggered the bad kernel.
[06:20] Zoe: ops question  do we want to run the next canary with the older compilation pipeline but new batching? that would help isolate.
[06:28] Laura: yes that would be clean isolation. but we should pin to single zone and simulate seq-length tail.
[06:34] Samir: decision: run isolated canaries, flip compiler revert in canary, keep batching change out until we validate. run smoke perf before routing traffic. agreed? (murmurs) yes.
[06:50] Priya: timeline implications for launch? We were aiming for mid-February public launch. If bisect and tests go fast we might keep timeframe; if not we shift two weeks. Need final signoff by Jan 20 from PM + Infra.
[07:05] Samir: ok add that to roadmap changes. I'll update gantt.
[07:10] Laura: technical ask  I need logs correlated at trace-id level across regions; Nate, can you enable trace-id debug sampling for the next 48hrs on staging?
[07:20] Nate: yes, but low sample rate  I'll turn on high sampling for the canary cluster.
[07:26] Miles: QA will need access to canary metrics and the perf-bench results; please share raw artifacts link.
[07:33] Samir: noted.
[07:36] (brief cross talk)
[07:50] Priya: on comms  if we delay launch, we need to update partners and sales with a technical note and expected timeline; I'll coordinate with AE leads. Also want to confirm messaging around rollback so we don't over-share internal failure details.
[08:05] Samir: agreed. keep it high-level: regression detected in canary, rollback applied, investigating, ETA for next canary by Jan 5.
[08:16] Laura: Ops follow-up: we should add version pinning per-zone in canary routing service and a metadata tag indicating compile pipeline.
[08:28] Zoe: will update runbooks and the pre-rollout checklist in Confluence.
[08:34] Miles: QA will add two new tests to the regression suite: 1) long-tail sequence load 2) streaming flush under KV churn.
[08:45] Samir: ok final recap and owners  Laura bisect + revert test (due 2027-01-05), Nate ops runbook + rollback automation (due 2026-12-28), Miles extended QA (due 2027-01-06), Priya comms + partner notes (due 2027-01-10), Samir update roadmap and coordinate PM signoff (due 2026-12-29).
[09:05] Samir: any blockers we didn't surface?
[09:10] Laura: just dependency on trace logs; once enabled I'll proceed.
[09:15] Nate: need 2 hours of ops review next Wed for the automation runbook.
[09:20] Priya: nothing else from PM.
[09:22] Samir: great, thanks everyone. We'll reconvene in one week for status and earlier if Laura has bisect results. Meeting adjourned.
